conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes that the claim is false and states that there is no evidence that drinking boiled garlic water cures COVID-19.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
**Conclusion: False.** There is no evidence that drinking boiled garlic water cures COVID-19. WHO states that although garlic has some antimicrobial properties, there is no evidence that eating garlic prevents COVID-19; therefore, it also does not establish boiled garlic water as a treatment or cure. WHO’s COVID-19 therapeutics guidance, rather than garlic, is the appropriate source for evidence-based treatment recommendations.

For people at higher risk of severe illness, CDC identifies authorized/approved antiviral medicines that can reduce hospitalization and death when used appropriately. Do not substitute garlic water for medical assessment or prescribed treatment, as doing so could delay effective care.

Garlic consumed orally can cause abdominal pain, gas, and nausea; garlic supplements can increase bleeding risk, especially relevant for people taking anticoagulant drugs. If you have COVID-19 symptoms or a positive test—particularly if you are older, pregnant, immunocompromised, or have chronic medical conditions—contact a clinician promptly to discuss eligibility for treatment.

Sources:  
- WHO: https://cdn.who.int/media/docs/default-source/searo/thailand/12myths-final.pdf?sfvrsn=76a26eb2_0  
- CDC: https://www.cdc.gov/covid/hcp/clinical-care/outpatient-treatment.html  
- NCCIH: https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/garlic
